belief: “I should have fought harder or left sooner. Because I didn’t, I must have agreed to it.”
belief_plain: I should have fought harder or left sooner. Because I didn’t, I must have agreed to it
origins: After harm, people torture themselves with the exit they can see now. “I should have fought harder. I should have left sooner. Because I didn’t, I agreed.” That uses today’s knowledge against the person you were then. Freezing, staying, hoping, having nowhere to go, loving someone, or being afraid are not consent. Not leaving is not the same thing as agreeing. You do not owe anyone a story of why you stayed. If you are not safe right now, call 911. You can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. If a child is being hurt, call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453. A counselor can help you at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do this alone, or all at once.
self: If I had been braver, it would have stopped.
A strong person would have left the first time.
I have no right to complain now.
God wanted me to endure it.
Leaving now would prove I could have left then, so I must not.
replacement: Not fighting or not leaving was not agreement. I survived the way I could, and that was not consent.
